newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia eyes foreign investments in tourism, oil.
newsitem.headline: Croatia eyes foreign investments in tourism, oil.

text.p: Croatia is in talks with South Korean concern Daewoo about a proposed $300 million investment into a hotel complex in Dubrovnik, Vanja Kalogjera, head of the Croatian Investment Promotion Agency (CIPA), said on Thursday.

Daewoo is interested in buying a five-hotel complex of Babin Kuk, estimated to be worth roughly $100 million, and investing another $200 million in its upgrading, Kalogjera told Reuters in an interview.
"The negotiations should be finished by the summer," Kalogjera said. "If the deal materialises, it would be one of the biggest direct foreign investments in Croatia so far."
He said foreign interest in investing in the country had increased considerably since the beginning of the year.

"The number of inquiries and concrete projects has more than doubled in the last three months. It seems foreigners have finally realised that Croatia is a safe place to invest with a stable macroeconomic situation and a very liberal legal system," Kalogjera said.
The National Bank of Croatia recently put total 1996 direct foreign investments at around $280 million.
In another deal expected to be struck soon, Austrian hotel operater Rogner is to buy hotel Imperial in Dubrovnik, damaged in a fire during a Serb artillery attack in 1991.
Rogner is supposed to invest between 35 and 40 million German marks in restoring the stylish old hotel, built by the Austrians a hundred years ago.
Croatia is also negotiating a number of separate deals with the Kuwaiti Investment Authority (KIA), Kalogjera said.

KIA was reportedly interested in acquiring a $50-million stake in Janaf, the operating company of the Adriatic crude oil pipeline that links the port of Rijeka and central Europe, and in investing into Croatian shipbuilding industry.
The talks for both packages are supposed to be completed by June, Kalogjera said.
In a another project, KIA and Zagreb's Montmontaza are negotiating a plan to build a shopping centre in the centre of Zagreb, worth 82 million German marks.

Kalogjera cited a number of smaller projects which are currently being negotiated or have already been closed in the fields of food processing, infrastructure, electronics and tourism with Italian, German and U.S. partners.
